notes.1: Side view and the woman is small. Her hand is open and short of the broom, so the grab has not happened.

notes.6: Quarter view with the face visible. Deep lunge into the corner and a clear hand gripping the broom. The corner and the whole action show.
notes.7: Side view of a deep lunge with a clear grab on the broom, and the corner shows. Her face is small and in profile, and the pose is less dynamic than in 6.

G001.reason: Cell 6 wins because it shows the full story in one view. She lunges deep into the corner, the corner is visible, and her hand grips the broom. A quarter view shows her face and the action together. Cell 7 also shows a clear grab in the corner, but it is a side view with a small face and a weaker lunge. Cells 1–4 only reach and do not grab, and cells 5 and 8 are too tight to show the place.

notes.1: The figure is tiny and far away, so you cannot read the face or the feeling. The long pier does show the stretch.

G002.reason: Cell 9 wins because the face and the calm pose are clear in a quarter view, and the long pier running into the sea, plus the far shore, show 'off the pier' and the stretch of time. Cell 5 has a clear peaceful face, but the extreme close-up cuts most of the pier and the sea. Cell 8 is clear too, but the man walks along the pier and the sea is less visible. Cell 2 is similar to 9, but its pier is short and the man looks up, so the stretch reads less. No cell shows the 'ended' part, so I picked the cell that carries the peace and the pier best.

G003.reason: Cell 9 wins because Carl's face, his knocking hand and the cat's head tilt all show in one medium shot, and the cat is close enough to Carl that the knock and the tilt read together. Cell 1 is the next best: the knock is clear, but the shot is wide, and Carl and the cat are small. Cell 8 is third, because the cat is far from Carl and his face is turned down toward the door.

G004.reason: Cell 1 wins because the face is a clear sly smirk in three-quarter view and the action reads at once. Both hands stuff ballots into the slot, and the wig, the box and the ballot stacks on the table all show. The next best, cell 4, shows the same action but looks down from above, so the face is partly hidden and the setting is thinner. It has the main actor in quarter view with her face visible, the headlamp beam, hands operating, the dark OR, and the spark that marks the power surge. Cell 9 is the next best: it also shows her operating by headlamp in a dark OR. But it has no spark, so the power cut is not clear, and she is smaller in the frame.

G006.reason: Cell 1 shows the whole story in one frame. The man's face is in three-quarter view, his hand is on the tab, and both quiet people are at the table with calm faces. G007.reason: Cell 1 wins because the smile, the light throw, the keys in flight and Tom's reaching hands all show in one medium shot. The two actors are of similar size and in a good view. G010.reason: Cell 1 wins because it combines a three-quarter view of the surgeon with the blade touching the scalp at a visible incision. The gleaming bald head and the patient's face show, so the whole sentence reads in one image. Cells 2 and 8 are the next best, but both are tight close-ups that lose the patient and the place, and the surgeon is blurred in cell 8.
